claim: The orientation of hair bundles on top of sensory hair cells in neuromasts of the lateral line system allows fish to detect direction of water flow.
source: The orientation of hair bundles on top of sensory hair cells (HCs) in neuromasts of the lateral line system allows fish to detect direction of water flow.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about the lateral line system.

claim: Each neuromast shows hair bundles arranged in two opposing directions.
source: Each neuromast shows hair bundles arranged in two opposing directions and each afferent neuron innervates only HCs of the same orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of neuromasts.

claim: Each afferent neuron innervates only HCs of the same orientation.
source: Each neuromast shows hair bundles arranged in two opposing directions and each afferent neuron innervates only HCs of the same orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of afferent neuron innervation patterns.

claim: Emx2 expression in half of the HCs mediates hair bundle reversal.
source: Previously, we showed that this opposition is established by expression of Emx2 in half of the HCs, where it mediates hair bundle reversal (Jiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Emx2 regulates neuronal selection such that afferent neurons innervate either Emx2-positive or negative HCs.
source: Here, we show that Emx2 also regulates neuronal selection: afferent neurons innervate either Emx2-positive or negative HCs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study stated in the abstract.

claim: In emx2 knockout neuromasts, all HCs are unidirectional.
source: In emx2 knockout and gain-of-function neuromasts, all HCs are unidirectional and the innervation patterns and physiological responses of the afferent neurons are dependent on the presence or absence of Emx2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an observation from the experimental data.

claim: In emx2 gain-of-function neuromasts, all HCs are unidirectional.
source: In emx2 knockout and gain-of-function neuromasts, all HCs are unidirectional and the innervation patterns and physiological responses of the afferent neurons are dependent on the presence or absence of Emx2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The innervation patterns of afferent neurons in emx2 mutants are dependent on the presence or absence of Emx2.
source: In emx2 knockout and gain-of-function neuromasts, all HCs are unidirectional and the innervation patterns and physiological responses of the afferent neurons are dependent on the presence or absence of Emx2.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: The physiological responses of afferent neurons in emx2 mutants are dependent on the presence or absence of Emx2.
source: In emx2 knockout and gain-of-function neuromasts, all HCs are unidirectional and the innervation patterns and physiological responses of the afferent neurons are dependent on the presence or absence of Emx2.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: Emx2 mediates the directional selectivity of neuromasts by regulating hair bundle orientation in HCs.
source: Our results indicate that Emx2 mediates the directional selectivity of neuromasts by two distinct processes: regulating hair bundle orientation in HCs and selecting afferent neuronal targets.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the study's findings.

claim: Emx2 mediates the directional selectivity of neuromasts by selecting afferent neuronal targets.
source: Our results indicate that Emx2 mediates the directional selectivity of neuromasts by two distinct processes: regulating hair bundle orientation in HCs and selecting afferent neuronal targets.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the study's findings.

claim: The lateral line system enables aquatic animals to sense water pressure and the direction of water flow.
source: Some aquatic animals have a specialized sensory organ or lateral line system that enables them to sense water pressure and the direction of water flow.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The lateral line system is important for prey detection, mating and predator avoidance.
source: The lateral line system is important for many survival behaviors such as prey detection, mating and predator avoidance (Coombs and Conley, 1997; Montgomery et al., 1997; Engelmann et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The lateral line system is comprised of individual neuromasts distributed over the surface of the body.
source: This sensory system is comprised of individual neuromasts distributed over the surface of the body (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Each neuromast consists of a cluster of sensory HCs that sense the direction of water flow bi-directionally along either the anterior-posterior or dorsal-ventral axis of the body.
source: Each neuromast consists of a cluster of sensory HCs that sense the direction of water flow bi-directionally along either the anterior-posterior (A-P) or dorsal-ventral (D-V) axis of the body (Ghysen and Dambly-Chaudière, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to previous work.

claim: Hair bundles that protrude from the top of HCs are structured asymmetrically to enable directional sensitivity.
source: First, specialized hair bundles that protrude from the top of the HCs are structured asymmetrically to enable directional sensitivity (Figure 1B; Flock and Wersall, 1962; López-Schier et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Each hair bundle is comprised of a staircase of actin-filled microvilli called stereocilia, located next to the kinocilium.
source: Each hair bundle is comprised of a staircase of actin-filled microvilli called stereocilia, located next to the kinocilium (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Deflections of the bundle towards its kinocilium open mechanotransduction channels on top of the stereocilia, allowing entry of positive ions and resulting in activation (depolarization) of the HC.
source: Only deflections of the bundle towards its kinocilium open mechanotransduction channels on top of the stereocilia, which allow entry of positive ions and result in activation (depolarization) of the HC (Figure 1B; Shotwell et al., 1981).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Deflections of the hair bundle away from its kinocilium close mechanotransduction channels and result in inhibition (hyperpolarization).
source: By contrast, deflections of the hair bundle in the opposite direction away from its kinocilium close mechanotransduction channels and result in inhibition (hyperpolarization).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The two opposite orientations of the hair bundles within a neuromast provide its bi-directional sensitivity.
source: Thus, the two opposite orientations of the hair bundles within a neuromast provide its bi-directional sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical conclusion from the preceding information.

claim: Neurons of the lateral line ganglion innervate neuromast HCs such that each neuron only innervates HCs that exhibit the same hair bundle orientation.
source: These neurons innervate neuromast HCs such that each neuron only innervates HCs that exhibit the same hair bundle orientation (Figure 1B; Nagiel et al., 2008; Faucherre et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Lateral line neurons select their HC targets independent of HC activity.
source: Although earlier results seem to be in conflict (Nagiel et al., 2009; Faucherre et al., 2010), more recent work has consistently concluded that lateral line neurons select their HC targets independent of HC activity, based on studies in mutants that lack HC mechanotransduction or neurotransmission (Nagiel et al., 2009; Pujol-Martí et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous studies.

claim: The molecular mechanism(s) that determine how directional selectivity is preserved at the level of neuronal innervation is not known.
source: However, the molecular mechanism(s) that determine how this directional selectivity is preserved at the level of neuronal innervation is not known.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Emx2 controls the orientation of hair bundles within neuromasts and vestibular maculae of the inner ear in both zebrafish and mice.
source: Previous results have demonstrated that the orientation of hair bundles within neuromasts as well as vestibular maculae of the inner ear in both zebrafish and mice is controlled by the transcription factor, Emx2 (Jiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to previous work.

claim: As each HC precursor divides to form two nascent HCs, Emx2 is only expressed in one of the two daughter cells.
source: In neuromasts, as each HC precursor divides to form two nascent HCs, Emx2 is only expressed in one of the two daughter cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a known fact from previous work.

claim: Emx2 is expressed in half of the HCs within a neuromast.
source: As a result, Emx2 is expressed in half of the HCs within a neuromast, and it functions to change the hair bundle orientation to approximately 180 degrees from the default state to generate a bi-directional hair bundle pattern (Jiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to previous work.

claim: Emx2 functions to change the hair bundle orientation to approximately 180 degrees from the default state to generate a bi-directional hair bundle pattern.
source: As a result, Emx2 is expressed in half of the HCs within a neuromast, and it functions to change the hair bundle orientation to approximately 180 degrees from the default state to generate a bi-directional hair bundle pattern (Jiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to previous work.

claim: In wildtype neuromasts, each afferent neuron only innervates either Emx2-positive or Emx2-negative HCs.
source: Based on these results, we hypothesized that each afferent neuron should only innervate either Emx2 positive or negative HCs within a neuromast (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This hypothesis is tested and confirmed by the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: In wildtype neuromasts, Emx2 immunoreactivities are only detected in mature HCs with hair bundles oriented towards the posterior direction (A > P).
source: As previously demonstrated, in these neuromasts, Emx2 immunoreactivities are only detected in mature HCs with hair bundles oriented towards the posterior direction (A > P, Figure 1C,F–J,K,N–R; Jiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Emx2 is expressed in immature HCs that can be identified by weak GFP signals and/or incomplete bundle polarity establishment.
source: Emx2 is also expressed in immature HCs that can be identified by weak GFP signals and/or incomplete bundle polarity establishment.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an observation from the data.

claim: Only one of the immature HCs within a pair expresses Emx2.
source: Only one of the immature HCs within a pair expresses Emx2 (Figure 1C–R, yellow arrow).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Each single-labeled neuron either associates with all the Emx2-positive HCs or all the Emx2-negative HCs in a neuromast.
source: Notably, we found that each single-labeled neuron either associated with all the Emx2-positive HCs in a neuromast (example, Figure 1C–J), or associated with all the Emx2-negative HCs in a neuromast (example, Figure 1K–R).
evidence: This is stated in the results and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: In wildtype neuromasts, fibers of a single-labeled neuroD:tdTomato-positive neuron only overlap with a subset of the HGn39D-GFP-positive afferents and ramify approximately one half of the neuromast.
source: In wildtype neuromasts, fibers of a single-labeled neuroD:tdTomato-positive neuron only overlapped with a subset of the HGn39D-GFP-positive afferents and ramified approximately one half of the neuromast (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In emx2 ko neuromasts, all HCs are oriented towards the anterior direction (P > A).
source: By contrast, emx2 ko neuromasts, in which all HCs are oriented towards the anterior direction (Figure 2E,I, P > A), showed an altered neuronal branching pattern (Figure 2F–H,J–L).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: emx2 ko neuromasts show an altered neuronal branching pattern.
source: By contrast, emx2 ko neuromasts, in which all HCs are oriented towards the anterior direction (Figure 2E,I, P > A), showed an altered neuronal branching pattern (Figure 2F–H,J–L).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The majority of single neurons in emx2 ko neuromasts show a broader distribution compared to controls.
source: The majority of the single neurons in emx2 ko neuromasts showed a broader distribution (Figure 2G), when compared to controls (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In wildtype fish, the overlap by a single neuron is consistently around 50%.
source: We quantified the average percentage of overlap between tdTomato- and GFP-positive areas and found that in wildtype fish, the overlap by a single neuron is consistently around 50% (Figure 2U, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2U and source data.

claim: Single neurons in emx2 ko segregate into two populations showing either dramatically more (70%) or less (20%) overlap than wildtype neurons.
source: In contrast, single neurons in emx2 ko clearly segregated into two populations and showed either dramatically more (70%) or less (20%) overlap than the wildtype neurons (Figure 2U, p=0.0016 for emx2 ko major, p=0.0012 for emx2 ko minor).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 2U.

claim: Similar major and minor branching patterns are observed for emx2 gof neuromasts.
source: Similar major (Figure 2N–P,U, p=0.0006) and minor (Figure 2R–T,U, p=0.0005) branching patterns were observed for emx2 gof neuromasts, in which all HCs are oriented in the A > P direction (Figure 2M,Q).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In emx2 gof neuromasts, all HCs are oriented in the A > P direction.
source: Similar major (Figure 2N–P,U, p=0.0006) and minor (Figure 2R–T,U, p=0.0005) branching patterns were observed for emx2 gof neuromasts, in which all HCs are oriented in the A > P direction (Figure 2M,Q).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The altered branching pattern of a single afferent neuron in both emx2 ko and gof mutants suggests that Emx2 regulates the pattern of neuronal innervation.
source: The altered branching pattern of a single afferent neuron in both emx2 ko and gof mutants suggests that in addition to establishing hair bundle orientation, Emx2 also regulates the pattern of neuronal innervation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In wildtype neuromasts, a single afferent contacts approximately half of the total HCs (52.9%).
source: Figure 3A–D3 illustrates a wildtype neuromast, in which a single afferent contacts all the HCs that are in a P > A orientation (Figure 3A–C, 4 out of 9 total HCs, Figure 3D-D3, arrowheads, Table 1, 52.9%, Table 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: In emx2 ko, major afferent neurons contact more than half (74.8%) of the total number of HCs within a neuromast.
source: In emx2 ko, major afferent neurons contacted more than half (Figure 3E–H3, 8 out of 10 total HCs, Table 1, 74.8%, p=5.19E-20, Table 1—source data 1) while minor afferent neurons contacted less than half of the total number of HCs within a neuromast (Figure 3I–L3, 4 out of 13 HCs, Table 1, 25.4%, p=1.41E-21, Table 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: In emx2 ko, minor afferent neurons contact less than half (25.4%) of the total number of HCs within a neuromast.
source: In emx2 ko, major afferent neurons contacted more than half (Figure 3E–H3, 8 out of 10 total HCs, Table 1, 74.8%, p=5.19E-20, Table 1—source data 1) while minor afferent neurons contacted less than half of the total number of HCs within a neuromast (Figure 3I–L3, 4 out of 13 HCs, Table 1, 25.4%, p=1.41E-21, Table 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: In emx2 gof neuromasts, major neurons contact 75.2% of HCs.
source: Similar to emx2 ko afferents, major and minor neurons contacted a significantly more and fewer HCs respectively in emx2 gof neuromasts compared to wildtype afferents (Example major, Figure 3M-P3, 10 out of 12 HCs, arrowheads, Table 1, 75.2%, p=1.82E-25; example minor, Figure 3Q-T2, 3 out of 11 HCs, arrowheads, Table 1, 25.8%, p=1.08E-18, Table 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: In emx2 gof neuromasts, minor neurons contact 25.8% of HCs.
source: Similar to emx2 ko afferents, major and minor neurons contacted a significantly more and fewer HCs respectively in emx2 gof neuromasts compared to wildtype afferents (Example major, Figure 3M-P3, 10 out of 12 HCs, arrowheads, Table 1, 75.2%, p=1.82E-25; example minor, Figure 3Q-T2, 3 out of 11 HCs, arrowheads, Table 1, 25.8%, p=1.08E-18, Table 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: The nerve endings of both major and minor neurons in emx2 mutants are juxtaposed to HC bodies similar to controls.
source: However, in emx2 mutants, the nerve endings of both major and minor neurons were juxtaposed to HC bodies (Figure 3H1–H3, L1–L3, P1–P3, T1–T2, arrowheads) similar to controls (Figure 3D1–D3), suggesting that they were successfully making HC contacts.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The frequency of major and minor single afferent neurons is in an approximate ratio of 3:2 for both emx2 ko and gof neuromasts.
source: We also examined the frequency of major and minor single afferent neurons obtained using single fiber labeling and found they were in an approximate respective ratio of 3:2, for both emx2 ko and gof neuromasts (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Table 1.

claim: In wildtype larvae, afferent fibers are associated with presynaptic RibeyeB staining.
source: In wildtype larvae, afferent fibers are associated with presynaptic RibeyeB staining (Figure 4B–D3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: In both emx2 ko and gof neuromasts, major and minor afferent neurons associate with RibeyeB-labeled presynapses.
source: In both emx2 ko and gof neuromasts, we observed that major as well as minor afferent neurons associated with RibeyeB-labeled presynapses (Figure 4E–T3, white arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Both major and minor afferent nerve endings in emx2 mutants are adjacent to presynapses but some fail to directly associate.
source: However, we also observed both major and minor afferent nerve endings that were adjacent to presynapses but failed to directly associate (Figure 4E–T3, white arrowheads).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The number of RibeyeB puncta colocalized with tdTomato-positive nerve endings per HC is not changed for major fibers but significantly decreased for minor fibers in emx2 mutants.
source: When we quantified the number of RibeyeB puncta that were colocalized with tdTomato-positive nerve endings per HC, we found that this number was not changed for the major fibers, but significantly decreased for the minor fibers for both loss- and gain-of-emx2 function neuromasts (Figure 4—source data 1, p=0.069 for emx2 ko major, p=0.007 for emx2 ko minor, p=0.383 for emx2 gof major, p=0.002 for emx2 gof minor).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and reference to source data.

claim: The Mander's colocalization coefficients are decreased in minor fibers of emx2 mutants compared to wildtype.
source: Consistent with fewer RibeyeB puncta associating with afferent fibers, the Mander's colocalization coefficients were also decreased in minor fibers of emx2 mutants compared to wildtype (Figure 4—source data 2, p=0.159 for emx2 ko major, p=0.048 for emx2 ko minor, p=0.011 for emx2 gof major, p=0.037 for emx2 gof minor).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and reference to source data.

claim: A majority of the afferent nerve endings in emx2 mutants and wildtype are associated with presynapses.
source: Together, these results suggest that a majority of the afferent nerve endings in emx2 mutants and wildtype are associated with presynapses.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Incomplete synapses are more prevalent in emx2 mutants than in wildtype, primarily in the minor fibers.
source: However, the presence of nerve endings juxtaposed to HC bodies that do not associate with presynapses (incomplete synapses) are more prevalent in the emx2 mutants than in wildtype (Sheets et al., 2017), primarily in the minor fibers.
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to previous work.

claim: In wildtype neuromasts, the majority of RibeyeB and Maguk puncta are juxtaposed with each other, with an average of three complete synapses per HC.
source: In wildtype neuromasts (Figure 5A–D2), the majority of RibeyeB and Maguk puncta were juxtaposed with each other, and based on this co-label, we observed on average three complete synapses per HC (Figure 5M; Sheets et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Similar numbers of complete synapses per HC are observed in both emx2 ko and gof mutants compared to wildtype.
source: Similar numbers of complete synapses per HC in both emx2 ko and gof mutants were observed (Figure 5E–H2, I–L2, M, p=0.103 for emx2 ko, p=0.878 for emx2 gof, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Using Mander's colocalization analysis, there is no difference in RibeyeB and Maguk overlap in emx2 mutants compared to wildtype.
source: We also used Mander's colocalization analysis to quantify the proportion of RibeyeB label that overlapped with Maguk label. Using this analysis, we found no difference in emx2 mutants, compared to wildtype (Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to source data.

claim: emx2 mutant neuromasts show an increase in both total RibeyeB and Maguk per HC.
source: Although there is no difference in complete synapse number and overall pre-and post-synaptic colocalization, emx2 mutant neuromasts showed an increase number of both total RibeyeB and Maguk per HC (p=6.09E-05 for RibeyeB of emx2 ko, p=2.09E-04 for RibeyeB of emx2 gof, p=3.35E-04 for Maguk of emx2 ko, p=0.567 for Maguk of emx2 gof, Figure 5—source data 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and reference to source data.

claim: There are significantly more solitary RibeyeB or Maguk puncta in both emx2 ko and gof mutants compared to controls.
source: We quantified the percentage of solitary RibeyeB or Maguk puncta per neuromast and found that there were significantly more solitary puncta in both emx2 ko and gof mutants compared to controls (Figure 5H–H2,L–L2, N, p=5.05E-07 for RibeyeB of emx2 ko, p=1.35E-08 for RibeyeB of emx2 gof, p=9.98E-09 for Maguk of emx2 ko, p=0.033 for Maguk of emx2 gof, Figure 5—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The uncoupling of pre- and post-synaptic components in emx2 mutants supports the idea that there are failures in synapse formation.
source: The uncoupling of pre- and post-synaptic components support that idea that in addition to forming authentic synapses, emx2 mutants also have failures in synapse formation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In wildtype, robust calcium signals are observed in the innervating afferent process during both A > P and P > A directed waterjet stimulation.
source: In wildtype, we observed robust calcium signals in the innervating afferent process during both A > P and P > A directed waterjet stimulation (Figure 6A,A').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In wildtype afferents, calcium responses to each directional stimulation (A > P or P > A) occur in distinct domains of the afferent process.
source: In wildtype afferents, calcium responses to each directional stimulation (A > P or P > A) occurred in distinct domains of the afferent process (Figure 6A,A').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Calcium signals in emx2 ko afferents are only observed in response to P > A stimulation.
source: In contrast, calcium signals were only observed in response to P > A stimulation in emx2 ko afferents (Figure 6B').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Calcium signals in emx2 gof afferents are only detected in response to A > P stimulations.
source: Inversely, calcium signals were only detected in response to A > P stimulations in emx2 gof afferents (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6.

claim: No afferent calcium signals are observed in emx2 ko mutants during A > P stimuli.
source: No afferent calcium signals were observed in emx2 ko mutants during A > P stimuli (Figure 6B) or in emx2 gof mutants during P > A stimuli (Figure 6C').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6.

claim: No afferent calcium signals are observed in emx2 gof mutants during P > A stimuli.
source: No afferent calcium signals were observed in emx2 ko mutants during A > P stimuli (Figure 6B) or in emx2 gof mutants during P > A stimuli (Figure 6C').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6.

claim: HCs and afferent neurons in emx2 mutants are functional and directionally selective.
source: These results indicate that HCs and afferent neurons in emx2 mutants are functional and directionally selective.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the calcium imaging data.

claim: For the A > P stimulus, the emx2 gof calcium signals are 41% higher compared to wildtype.
source: We found that for the A > P stimulus, the emx2 gof calcium signals were 41% higher compared to wildtype (Figure 6D,D', p=0.027, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In emx2 ko fish, the P > A calcium signals are 58% higher compared to wildtype.
source: Similarly, in emx2 ko fish, the P > A calcium signals were 58% higher compared to wildtype (Figure 6E,E', p=0.0003, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Compared to wildtype, in emx2 mutants, afferents are able to recruit additional HCs to respond to their respective direction of stimulus.
source: These results suggest that compared to wildtype, in emx2 mutants, afferents are able to recruit additional HCs to respond to their respective direction of stimulus.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the calcium imaging data.

claim: Per HC, the magnitude of the afferent calcium signal is the same in emx2 mutants compared to wildtype.
source: Using this approach, we found that per HC, the magnitude of the afferent calcium signal was the same compared to wildtype (Figure 6F,G, A > P direction: GCaMP6 ∆F/F, wildtype 70.5%, emx2 ko 71.6%, p=0.99; P > A direction: GCaMP6 ∆F/F, wildtype 51.6%, emx2 gof 73.4%, p=0.48, Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The overall properties of each HC-afferent contact are not dramatically altered in emx2 mutants.
source: This suggests that the overall properties of each HC-afferent contact are not dramatically altered in emx2 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the calcium imaging data.

claim: In wildtype larvae, trains of action potentials (spikes) can be recorded either during A > P or P > A stimuli in wildtype afferents.
source: Consistent with this sensitivity pattern, during a 500 ms waterjet stimulus, we were able to record trains of action potentials (spikes) either during A > P or P > A stimuli in wildtype afferents (Figure 7A,B, wildtype, A > P, 5/15, 33%, P > A, 10/15, 66%, n = 15 afferent neurons, Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7.

claim: When wildtype afferents are stimulated in the opposite directions (off-stimulus direction), the average spike number is dramatically reduced.
source: When these same wildtype afferents were stimulated in the opposite directions (off-stimulus direction), the average spike number was dramatically reduced (Figure 7B').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Only P > A afferents are identified in emx2 ko mutants.
source: When we recorded spikes in emx2 mutant afferent neurons, we only identified P > A afferents in emx2 ko mutants (n = 8/8 neurons; Figure 7B) and A > P afferents in emx2 gof mutants (n = 7/7 neurons; Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Only A > P afferents are identified in emx2 gof mutants.
source: When we recorded spikes in emx2 mutant afferent neurons, we only identified P > A afferents in emx2 ko mutants (n = 8/8 neurons; Figure 7B) and A > P afferents in emx2 gof mutants (n = 7/7 neurons; Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7.

claim: The number of spikes in the on-stimulus direction in emx2 mutants is not greater than wildtype.
source: The number of spikes in the on-stimulus direction, in emx2 mutants was not greater than wildtype (wildtype versus emx2 ko, p=0.65; wildtype versus emx2 gof, p=0.74).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis.

claim: When emx2 mutant afferents are stimulated in the off-stimulus direction, the spike numbers are dramatically reduced, similar to wildtype afferents.
source: When emx2 mutant afferents were stimulated in the off-stimulus direction, similar to wildtype afferents, the spike numbers were dramatically reduced (Figure 7B').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Calcium imaging and electrophysiological results both indicate that the afferent neurons in emx2 mutants are functional and respond in a predicted manner according to their hair bundle orientation.
source: Together, our calcium imaging and electrophysiological results both indicate that the afferent neurons in emx2 mutants are functional and respond in a predicted manner according to their hair bundle orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary of the functional data.

claim: Hair bundles in neuromasts of vangl2m209 are misoriented due to misalignment of the basal body and the associated kinocilium.
source: Hair bundles in neuromasts of vangl2m209 are misoriented due to misalignment of the basal body and in turn the associated kinocilium, which directs bundle orientation during development (Figure 8E,M,P; López-Schier and Hudspeth, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation and shown in Figure 8.

claim: Although hair bundle orientation is random in vangl2m209 mutants, Emx2 is still expressed in half of the HCs within a neuromast.
source: Our results showed that although hair bundle orientation is random in vangl2m209 mutants, Emx2 is still expressed in half of the HCs within a neuromast (Figure 8E–H2, example 4/8 HCs, Figure 8I, p=0.67, Figure 8—source data 1), similar to controls (Figure 8A–D2, example 6/12 HCs, Figure 8I).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 8.

claim: The maintenance of 50% of Emx2-positive HCs in vangl2m209 mutants suggests that hair bundle misorientation in this mutant is independent of emx2.
source: The maintenance of 50% of Emx2-positive HCs in vangl2m209 mutants suggests that hair bundle misorientation in this mutant is independent of emx2 (Figure 8I).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The hair bundle orientation of double mutants of vangl2m209 with emx2 ko or gof is random.
source: Furthermore, the hair bundle orientation of double mutants of vangl2m209 with emx2 ko or gof was also random (Figure 8N,O).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8.

claim: The orientation defects in the double mutants resemble defects in vangl2m209, rather than the unidirectional orientation phenotype observed in emx2 ko and gof single mutants.
source: The orientation defects in the double mutants resembled defects in vangl2m209 (Figure 8M), rather than the unidirectional orientation phenotype observed in emx2 ko and gof single mutants (Figure 8K,L).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8.

claim: vangl2 is epistatic to emx2.
source: Therefore, these genetic analyses indicate that vangl2 is epistatic to emx2.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the genetic analysis.

claim: In vangl2m209 neuromasts, Emx2-mediated afferent selectivity is preserved.
source: When we examined the innervation patterns of single afferent neurons in vangl2m209 neuromasts, we observed that Emx2-mediated afferent selectivity was preserved.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an observation from the data.

claim: A single afferent neuron in vangl2m209 can selectively innervate Emx2-positive HCs.
source: For example, a single afferent neuron can selectively innervate Emx2-positive HCs (Example, Figure 8P–U, 5 out of 12 total HCs, circles).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8.

claim: The ratio of the number of HCs innervated by a single neuron within a vangl2m209 neuromast is similar to wildtype.
source: In addition, the ratio of the number of HCs innervated by a single neuron within a neuromast is similar to wildtype (Figure 8Y, p=0.26, Figure 8—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 8.

claim: Single neurons in vangl2m209 are able to select and contact only the Emx2-positive HCs, despite the misoriented hair bundles.
source: Importantly, single neurons were able to select and contact only the Emx2-positive HCs (Figure 8T–X), despite the misoriented hair bundles.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8.

claim: Neuronal innervation in neuromasts occurs independent of hair bundle orientation and is directed by Emx2.
source: These results indicate that neuronal innervation in neuromasts occurs independent of hair bundle orientation and is directed by Emx2.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the vangl2m209 data.

claim: In emx2 ko and gof neuromasts, one population of afferent neurons can innervate more than half of the total number of HCs.
source: In emx2 ko and gof neuromasts, in which all HCs have uni-directionally oriented bundles, we found that one population of afferent neurons can innervate more than half of the total number of HCs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Neurons have the capacity to innervate additional HCs of similar orientation based upon their availability.
source: These results suggest that these neurons have the capacity to innervate additional HCs of similar orientation based upon their availability.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: There is an upper limit to the capacity of a single neuron to innervate HCs since a single neuron was unable to innervate all the HCs within a ko or gof emx2 mutant neuromast.
source: Nevertheless, our results also suggest that there is an upper limit to this capacity since a single neuron was unable to innervate all the HCs within a ko or gof emx2 mutant neuromast.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Neurons that innervate Emx2-positive and -negative HCs in the mammalian maculae of the inner ear are most likely different from each other because their central axons project to different regions of the brain.
source: In support of this notion, neurons that innervate Emx2-positive and -negative HCs in the mammalian maculae of the inner ear are most likely different from each other because their central axons project to different regions of the brain (Maklad et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation to previous work.

claim: Neurons that innervate Emx2-positive and negative HCs in the lateral line system may be molecularly different, similar to the neurons of the mouse maculae.
source: Therefore, neurons that innervate Emx2-positive and negative HCs in the lateral line system may also be molecularly different, similar to the neurons of the mouse maculae.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on analogy.

claim: Specific synapse formation often requires partnering between pre- and post-synaptic signaling molecules such as ephrin-eph, semaphorin-plexin and other adhesion molecules.
source: Additionally, ample evidence from other systems indicates that specific synapse formation often requires partnering between pre- and post-synaptic signaling molecules such as ephrin-eph, semaphorin-plexin and other adhesion molecules (for review see, Sanes and Yamagata, 2009; Margeta and Shen, 2010; Williams et al., 2010; Yogev and Shen, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to review articles.

claim: The selective innervation pattern of the lateral line afferent neurons may be analogous to other pre- and postsynaptic neuronal pairing, requiring a match between the HCs and respective molecular determinants from the postsynaptic afferent neurons.
source: The selective innervation pattern of the lateral line afferent neurons may be analogous to other pre- and postsynaptic neuronal pairing, requiring a match between the HCs (expressing downstream effectors of Emx2 or the lack thereof) and respective molecular determinants from the postsynaptic afferent neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on analogy to other systems.

claim: Previous axotomy studies showed that when all axons innervating a single neuromast were severed except one, the single remaining neuron was able to expand its innervation to HCs of the opposite orientation.
source: Previous axotomy studies showed that when all axons innervating a single neuromast were severed except one, the single remaining neuron was able to expand its innervation to HCs of the opposite orientation (Pujol-Martí et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation to previous work.

claim: As a result of expanded innervation after axotomy, the remaining neuron responded to hair bundle deflections from two directions instead of one.
source: As a result of this expanded innervation, the remaining neuron responded to hair bundle deflections from two directions instead of one.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of previous findings.

claim: The axotomy data taken together with data on emx2 mutants suggest that other permissive factor(s) in addition to Emx2 instruct synapse formation and can expand innervations beyond their intended targets.
source: If we assume that there are indeed two types of neurons innervating a given neuromast, then the axotomy data taken together with our data on emx2 mutants suggest that other permissive factor(s) in addition to Emx2 instruct synapse formation and can expand innervations beyond their intended targets.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation combining current and previous findings.

claim: Neurons of the emx2 ko neuromasts only respond to stimulation in the P > A direction because only P > A HCs are present.
source: Despite the altered innervation pattern observed in the emx2 mutant neuromasts, our calcium imaging and extracellular neuronal recording results indicate that these neurons respond in the predicted manner according to the orientation of the HCs that they innervate; neurons of the emx2 ko neuromasts only respond to stimulation in the P > A direction because only P > A HCs are present.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the functional findings.

claim: Neurons of emx2 gof neuromasts only respond to hair bundle stimulation in the A > P direction.
source: Likewise, neurons of emx2 gof neuromasts only respond to hair bundle stimulation in the A > P direction.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the functional findings.

claim: The increase in post-synaptic calcium signals within the entire afferent terminal in emx2 mutants did not translate into more evoked spikes at the level of a single afferent neuron.
source: Despite the increase in the amplitude of post-synaptic calcium signals within the entire afferent terminal in emx2 mutant compared to controls, this increase did not translate into more evoked spikes at the level of a single afferent neuron, even though some of the neurons innervated more HCs than normal.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an observation from the data.

claim: Results from the vangl2m209 mutants suggest that neuronal selectivity is not dependent on hair bundle orientation per se.
source: However, results from the vangl2m209 mutants suggest that neuronal selectivity is not dependent on hair bundle orientation per se.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the vangl2m209 data.

claim: The neuronal innervation pattern in vangl2m209 remains consistent with the Emx2 expression pattern of HCs.
source: Although the mechanism of hair bundle misorientation in both vangl2m209 and emx2 mutant mice may share a common pathway (López-Schier and Hudspeth, 2006; Jiang et al., 2017), the neuronal innervation pattern in vangl2m209 remains consistent with the Emx2 expression pattern of HCs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations.

claim: Emx2 regulates both hair bundle orientation and neuronal innervation patterns, whereas Vangl2 only regulates hair bundle orientation.
source: These results suggest that Emx2 regulates both hair bundle orientation and neuronal innervation patterns, whereas Vangl2 only regulates hair bundle orientation, suggesting that these two cellular processes are independently regulated.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Emx2 expression in HCs of neuromasts is not affected in the vangl2m209.
source: Our results indicate that Emx2 expression in HCs of neuromasts is not affected in the vangl2m209 (Figure 8) and similarly, Vangl2 expression is not affected in Emx2 ko mouse inner ears (Jiang et al., 2017), further supporting that these proteins are independently regulated.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with reference to Figure 8 and citation.

claim: Vangl2 expression is not affected in Emx2 ko mouse inner ears.
source: Our results indicate that Emx2 expression in HCs of neuromasts is not affected in the vangl2m209 (Figure 8) and similarly, Vangl2 expression is not affected in Emx2 ko mouse inner ears (Jiang et al., 2017), further supporting that these proteins are independently regulated.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation.

claim: Genetic analyses indicate that vangl2 function is epistatic to emx2 with regards to hair bundle orientation.
source: However, our genetic analyses indicate that vangl2 function is epistatic to emx2 with regards to hair bundle orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the genetic analysis.

claim: A core planar cell polarity protein such as Vangl2 functions in an intercellular manner and regulates an intracellular signaling mechanism such as Emx2.
source: These results are consistent with results in the mouse utricle indicating that a core planar cell polarity protein such as Vangl2, functions in an intercellular manner and regulates an intracellular signaling mechanism such as Emx2 (Montcouquiol et al., 2006; Yin et al., 2012; Copley et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to previous work.

claim: The restricted expression of Emx2 to half of the HCs within a neuromast reverses the hair bundle orientation by 180 degrees and allows the detection of water flow from the opposite direction.
source: Taken together our results indicate that the restricted expression of Emx2 to half of the HCs within a neuromast reverses the hair bundle orientation by 180 degrees and allows the detection of water flow from the opposite direction (Jiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation.

claim: The expression of Emx2 guides neuronal patterning and preserves the directional selectivity of the HCs.
source: In addition, the expression of Emx2 guides neuronal patterning and preserves the directional selectivity of the HCs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Emx2 regulates the two key components that confer directional selectivity in the peripheral lateral line system.
source: Thus, Emx2 regulates the two key components that confer directional selectivity in the peripheral lateral line system.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary conclusion.

claim: Given the conserved role of Emx2 in mediating hair bundle orientation among mechanosensory organs of fish and mammals, its role in regulating post-synaptic partner may apply to other neural systems where Emx2 is normally expressed such as the cortex and olfactory epithelium.
source: Given the conserved role of Emx2 in mediating hair bundle orientation among mechanosensory organs of fish and mammals (Jiang et al., 2017), its role in regulating post-synaptic partner described here may apply to other neural systems where Emx2 is normally expressed such as the cortex and olfactory epithelium (Cecchi and Boncinelli, 2000; Cecchi, 2002; Nédélec et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations as speculation about broader implications.

claim: Neuronal selectivity is not dependent on hair bundle orientation.
source: However, neuronal selectivity is not dependent on hair bundle orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion from the study.

claim: In vangl2m209 mutants, in which hair bundles are randomly oriented, afferent neurons still segregate according to Emx2-positive and -negative HCs.
source: In vangl2m209 mutants, in which hair bundles are randomly oriented, afferent neurons still segregate according to Emx2-positive and -negative HCs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a key finding.
